'''XiaoFeng Wang''' ({{Lang-zh|s=王晓峰|p=Wáng Xiǎofēng}}) is a Chinese-American<ref name=IPM2/> computer scientist known for his research on computer security, cryptography, and privacy. Wang joined the faculty of [[Indiana University Bloomington]] (IU) in 2004. He was appointed as a full professor in 2015 and as the associate dean for research in 2023 at IU's [[Luddy School of Informatics, Computing, and Engineering]].<ref name=goodin-incommunicado>{{Cite web |last=Goodin |first=Dan |date=March 30, 2025 |title=FBI raids home of prominent computer scientist who has gone incommunicado |url=https://arstechnica.com/security/2025/03/computer-scientist-goes-silent-after-fbi-raid-and-purging-from-university-website/ |access-date=March 31, 2025 |website=[[Ars&nbsp;Technica]] |language=en-US |archive-date=March 31, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250331002237/https://arstechnica.com/security/2025/03/computer-scientist-goes-silent-after-fbi-raid-and-purging-from-university-website/ |url-status=live |quote=In recent weeks, Wang's email account, phone number, and profile page at the Luddy School were quietly erased by his employer. Over the same time, Indiana University also removed a profile for his wife, Nianli Ma, who was listed as a Lead Systems Analyst and Programmer at the university's Library Technologies division. ... 'None of this is in any way normal', Matthew Green, a professor specializing in cryptography at Johns Hopkins University, wrote on Mastodon. He continued: 'Has anyone been in contact? I hear he's been missing for two weeks and his students can't reach him. How does this not get noticed for two weeks???'}}</ref> He is now a professor at [[Nanyang Technological University]] in [[Singapore]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof Xiaofeng Wang |url=https://dr.ntu.edu.sg/entities/person/Wang-Xiaofeng |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260306172041/https://dr.ntu.edu.sg/entities/person/Wang-Xiaofeng |archive-date=Mar 6, 2026 |access-date=Mar 6, 2026 |website=Nanyang Technological University Singapore}}</ref>

In March 2025, Wang told IU he was planning to accept a position at another university after the end of the current academic year, and IU responded by putting him on [[administrative leave]], locking him out of his office and laptop, disabling his email account, removing his faculty profile and contact information from the university website, and then firing him from his position by email a couple of weeks later without providing a reason for his dismissal.<!-- The letter of termination did not say why he was being being terminated "effective immediately". --> His wife, who also worked at IU, was similarly dismissed by email without explanation. On the same day he was fired, his two homes were searched by the United States [[FBI]] and [[Department of Homeland Security]] federal agencies. It was later reported that the university has been investigating whether Wang had properly revealed who he was collaborating with and the sources of the funding for his research{{snd}} including whether he was receiving funding from China. Neither he nor his wife were arrested or charged with any crime. The [[American Association of University Professors|faculty labor union]] and more than 250 members of the IU faculty and staff have protested the manner of his dismissal, including at least 32 faculty members of the computer science department.

== Biography ==

=== Education ===
Wang received a [[Bachelor of Engineering]] in computer science from the [[Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics]] in 1993, a [[Master of Engineering]] in computer science from [[Shanghai Jiao Tong University]] in 1996, and a Doctor of Philosophy in electrical and computer engineering from [[Carnegie Mellon University]] in 2004.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=XiaoFeng Wang – Curriculum Vitae |url=https://homes.luddy.indiana.edu/xw7/CV.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240721214735/https://homes.luddy.indiana.edu/xw7/CV.pdf |archive-date=July 21, 2024 |access-date=July 21, 2024 |website=Indiana University School of Informatics, Computing and Engineering}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Department of Computer Science at North Carolina State University |url=https://www.csc.ncsu.edu/research/colloquia/seminar-post.php?id=388 |access-date=March 31, 2025 |website=www.csc.ncsu.edu |archive-date=March 31, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250331180206/https://www.csc.ncsu.edu/research/colloquia/seminar-post.php?id=388 |url-status=dead }}</ref> His doctoral dissertation is titled ''Multiagent coordination under untrusted and uncertain environments'' (2004).<ref name=":0" /> His doctoral advisor was [[Pradeep Khosla]], currently serving as the eighth chancellor of the [[University of California, San Diego]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Multiagent Coordination Under Untrusted and Uncertain Environments |url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/305202662 |access-date=March 31, 2025 |website=[[ProQuest]] |id={{ProQuest|305202662}} |language=en |url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=About the Chancellor |url=https://chancellor.ucsd.edu/about/about-the-chancellor/index.html |access-date=March 31, 2025 |website=[[University of California, San Diego]] |archive-date=March 26, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250326050851/https://chancellor.ucsd.edu/about/about-the-chancellor/index.html |url-status=live }}<!-- This source serves only to establish that Khosla is the chancellor. It does not mention Wang or his thesis. --></ref>

=== Career ===
After PhD graduation, Wang joined Indiana University Bloomington's [[Luddy School of Informatics, Computing, and Engineering|School of Informatics, Computing and Engineering]] in 2004 as a faculty member. He served as assistant professor from 2004 to 2010, as associate professor from 2010 to 2015, and as full professor from 2015 to 2025.<ref name=":1" /> He was named the James H. Rudy Professor of Computer Science, Engineering, and Informatics in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |title=IU cybersecurity researchers awarded multi-institutional NSF grants to protect data, user privacy |url=https://news.iu.edu/live/news/28018-iu-cybersecurity-researchers-awarded |access-date=March 31, 2025 |website=news.iu.edu |language=en}}</ref>

Wang was the lead principal investigator for the [[National Science Foundation]] (NSF) Center for Distributed Confidential Computing.<ref name=CDCC>{{cite web |url=https://nsf-cdcc.org/principle-investigators/ |title=Center for Distributed Confidential Computing |website=Center for Distributed Confidential Computing |access-date=April 16, 2025}}</ref> This NSF project in secure and trustworthy computing involved faculty from IU (the lead), Carnegie Mellon University, [[Duke University]], [[Ohio State University]], [[Penn State]], [[Purdue University]], [[Spelman College]], and [[Yale University]].<ref name="iualliance">{{cite web |title=Xiaofeng Wang |url=https://alliance.iu.edu/members/member/8580.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240911122716/https://alliance.iu.edu/members/member/8580.html |archive-date=September 11, 2024 |access-date=March 29, 2025 |website=Indiana University Alliance of Distinguished and Titled Professors}}</ref> Wang was also the director of Indiana University's Center for Security and Privacy in Informatics, Computing, and Engineering (SPICE).<ref name="iualliance" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Siek, Wang named ACM Distinguished Members |url=https://news.luddy.indiana.edu/story.html?story=Siek-Wang-named-ACM-Distinguished-Members |access-date=March 31, 2025 |website=Luddy School of Informatics, Computing, and Engineering: News Archive |language=en-US |archive-date=March 31, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250331034412/https://news.luddy.indiana.edu/story.html?story=Siek-Wang-named-ACM-Distinguished-Members |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In the ACM, Wang has been the chair of the Special Interest Group on Security, Audit and Control (SIGSAC).<ref name="SIGSAC">{{cite web |url=https://www.sigsac.org/ |title=ACM Special Interest Group on Security, Audit and Control (SIGSAC) – Chairman: XiaoFeng Wang |access-date=March 31, 2025 |website=[[Association for Computing Machinery]]}}</ref>

As of early March 2025, Wang was the associate dean for research; the James H. Rudy Professor of Computer Science, Engineering and Informatics; the director of Center for Security and Privacy in Informatics, Computing, and Engineering; and the director of Secure Computing at IU.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Profile – XiaoFeng Wang |url=https://cs.indiana.edu/contact/profile/?XiaoFeng_Wang |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250331013058/https://cs.indiana.edu/contact/profile/?XiaoFeng_Wang |archive-date=March 31, 2025 |access-date=March 29, 2025 |website=Indiana University Bloomington }}</ref>

=== 2025 firing from university and investigation by FBI ===
Approximately on March 14, 2025, the university removed his profile and the profile of his wife and their contact information from its website, and his whereabouts became unknown to his students.<ref name="goodin-incommunicado" /><ref name=IPM/> The university did not explain its action, but it was later reported that the university had been investigating whether Wang had properly revealed who he was collaborating with and the sources of the funding for his research{{snd}} including whether he was receiving funding from China.<ref name="goodin-incommunicado" /><ref name=WiredFunding/> Wang had been notified in mid-February 2025 that someone had made misconduct allegations against him, saying he had misidentified the principal investigator for a grant and failed to disclose some co-authors of his research, and the university had opened a formal investigation by March.<ref name=ProfAccused>{{cite web |url=https://indianapublicmedia.org/news/fired-prof-accused-of-research-misconduct-fbi-involvement-unclear.php |title=Fired prof accused of research misconduct, FBI involvement unclear |date=April 1, 2025 |first=Ethan |last=Sandweiss |website=[[Indiana Public Media]] |access-date=April 18, 2025 |archive-date=April 21, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250421091927/https://indianapublicmedia.org/news/fired-prof-accused-of-research-misconduct-fbi-involvement-unclear.php |url-status=dead }}</ref> Asked about these allegations, Alex Tanford, the president of the IU Bloomington chapter of the American Association of University Professors, said "While these are technical violations of research protocols, they're not serious and they happen all the time."<ref name=ProfAccused/> Tanford said that such allegations could raise concern and warrant investigation, but without a presumption of guilt for serious research misconduct.<ref name=ProfAccused/>

On March 24, 2025, Wang's wife, whose position at the university did not include tenure, was fired from her position by email and notified that she would not be eligible to be rehired, with no reason given for her dismissal.<ref name=Terminated4days>{{cite web |first1=Emerson |last1=Elledge |first2=Andrew |last2=Miller |url=https://www.idsnews.com/article/2025/04/nianli-ma-wang-xiaofeng-fbi-iu |title=Nianli Ma terminated 4 days before FBI searched her and Xiaofeng Wang's homes |date=April 10, 2025 |website=[[Indiana Daily Student]]}}</ref><ref name=AttorneyArgues>{{cite web |url=https://www.idsnews.com/article/2025/04/xiaofeng-wang-nianli-ma-warrant-fbi |title=U.S. attorney argues to keep search warrants for Xiaofeng Wang's home searches sealed |date=April 17, 2025 |first=Emerson |last=Elledge |website=[[Indiana Daily Student]]}}</ref><ref name=IPM2>{{cite web |url=https://indianapublicmedia.org/news/wangs-wife-asks-what-have-we-done-to-deserve-this-treatment.php |title=Wang's wife asks 'What have we done to deserve this treatment?' |website=[[Indiana Public Media]] |date=April 15, 2025 |quote=In her first public appearance since she and her husband were fired from Indiana University – and their homes were searched by the FBI – Nianli Ma said they are 'loyal Chinese-Americans and lawful immigrants'. |access-date=April 16, 2025 |archive-date=April 15, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250415193835/https://indianapublicmedia.org/news/wangs-wife-asks-what-have-we-done-to-deserve-this-treatment.php |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.idsnews.com/article/2025/04/xiaofeng-wang-iu-luddy-china-grant |title=IU's investigation on Xiaofeng Wang stems from 2017-18 Chinese grant, document says |first=Andrew |last=Miller |date=April 3, 2025 |website=[[Indiana Daily Student]]}}</ref>

On March 28, 2025, Wang's homes in [[Bloomington, Indiana|Bloomington]] and [[Carmel, Indiana|Carmel]], Indiana, were searched by the [[Federal Bureau of Investigation]] and the [[United States Department of Homeland Security]], and he was fired from the university on the same day.<ref name="heraldtimes">{{Cite web |last=Lane |first=Laura |title=FBI, Homeland Security agents search house on Xavier Court in Bloomington |date=March 28, 2025 |url=https://eu.heraldtimesonline.com/story/news/local/2025/03/28/fbi-department-of-homeland-security-agents-search-house-in-bloomington-indiana/82710451007/ |access-date=March 31, 2025 |website=[[The Herald-Times]]}}</ref><ref name=goodin-incommunicado/><ref name=cnbc-union>{{Cite web |last=Mangan |first=Dan |date=March 31, 2025 |title=Indiana U. fired cybersecurity professor XiaoFeng Wang on day FBI searched his homes: Union |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2025/03/31/fbi-searches-xiaofeng-wang-homes-indiana-university-cyrptography-computer.html |access-date=April 1, 2025 |website=CNBC |language=en}}</ref> The notification that he had been fired was sent to him in a message sent only by email<!-- The letter says "SENT VIA EMAIL ONLY" at the top in all-caps. --> from university executive vice president and [[Provost (education)|provost]] Rahul Shrivastav that said his employment was being terminated "effective immediately". The dismissal letter noted that Wang had informed the university of his intent to accept a new position at a different university and said he would be ineligible to be rehired by IU, but did not provide an explicit reason for his immediate dismissal.<ref name=WiredFunding/><ref name=cnbc-union/><ref name=DismissalLetter>{{cite web |url=https://www.documentcloud.org/documents/25874530-wangx-terminationmarch282029-1/?mode=document |title=Dear Professor Wang |via=[[DocumentCloud]] |date=March 28, 2025 |first=Rahul |last=Shrivastav |quote=SENT VIA EMAIL ONLY; Dear Professor Wang, I am writing to advise you that Indiana University has decided to terminate your employment effective immediately. ...}}<!-- Letter copy linked in the IPM Sandweiss article of March 31, 2025. --></ref>

The [[search warrant]]s were initially sealed, and Riana Pfefferkorn, a researcher at the [[Stanford University]] Institute for Human-Centered AI, filed a motion asking the court to unseal them.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 2, 2025 |title='Both are currently safe' {{!}} Lawyers confirm fired IU professor and wife are safe after FBI raids |url=https://www.wthr.com/article/news/crime/iu-professor-allegedly-accepted-job-in-singapore-before-firing-fbi-raids-xiaofeng-wang-singapore-indiana-university-job-terminated-fired-provost/531-2da4e241-5855-4e22-97d2-10b26951106d |access-date=April 3, 2025 |website=[[WTHR 13]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=IPM3/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.idsnews.com/article/2025/04/xiaofeng-wang-iu-warrants-stanford-motion |title=Stanford scholar files motion to unseal warrants used to search homes of Xiaofeng Wang |date=April 2, 2025 |first1=Marissa |last1=Meador |first2=Andrew |last2=Miller |website=[[Indiana Daily Student]]}}</ref> The acting [[U.S. attorney]] of the [[Southern District of Indiana]], [[John E. Childress]], filed a response on April 17, arguing for continued secrecy.<ref name=AttorneyArgues/> Wang's [[American Association of University Professors|union]] representative had communicated with him as early as March 28, 2025, and a defense lawyer was present at his home during the search.<ref name=goodin-incommunicado/><ref name=cnbc-union/> On April 2, 2025, a defense attorney made a statement on his behalf, saying that neither Wang nor his spouse had been arrested or charged with a crime.<ref name=dailystudent>{{Cite web|last=Miller |first=Andrew|title=IU professor and library analyst face no pending criminal charges, lawyers say |date=April 2, 2025 |url=https://www.idsnews.com/article/2025/04/iu-professor-no-criminal-charges-arrest-fbi-raid |access-date=April 2, 2025 |website=[[Indiana Daily Student]]|quote=Several of Wang's colleagues were unaware that he was under investigation by IU and gave different dates in March of him being placed on 'administrative leave'. Alex Tanford, American Association of University Professors IU Bloomington chapter president, told the IDS on Monday [March 31] that Wang had been placed on an 'interim administrative action' in mid-March, meaning he had been locked out from his office and laptop.}}</ref> On May 13, 2025, a judge ordered the U.S. Attorney to "show&nbsp;cause" for keeping the warrants sealed and to propose a redacted version of the warrant materials by May 27.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://indianapublicmedia.org/news/judge-says-feds-must-show-why-wang-warrants-must-stay-sealed.php |title=Judge says feds must show why Wang warrants must stay sealed |first=Ethan |last=Sandweiss |website=[[Indiana Public Media]] |date=May 14, 2025 |archive-date=May 20, 2025 |access-date=May 20, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250520063322/https://indianapublicmedia.org/news/judge-says-feds-must-show-why-wang-warrants-must-stay-sealed.php |url-status=dead }}</ref> Wang and his wife joined in requesting the unsealing of the search warrants on June 2.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.wfyi.org/news/articles/wang-moves-to-join-court-fight-to-unseal-warrants-used-to-search-his-homes |first=Ethan |last=Sandweiss |work=[[WFYI (TV)|WFYI]] |title=Wang moves to join court fight to unseal warrants used to search his homes |date=June 4, 2025}}</ref> 

On March 31, 2025, the Bloomington chapter of the [[American Association of University Professors]] sent a letter to IU saying that the university administration had fired Wang without due process and against the codified university policy and that he should be reinstated to the faculty.<ref name=cnbc-union/><ref><!-- Letter link found in CNBC article -->{{cite web |url=https://aaup.sitehost.iu.edu/reports/AAUP_March_31_Letter_Shrivastav.pdf |title=Dear Provost Shrivastav |date=March 31, 2025 |author=IUB-AAUP Executive Committee: Alex Tanford (Law), President |display-authors=etal |website=[[American Association of University Professors]] Indiana University Bloomington Chapter |access-date=April 18, 2025 |archive-date=April 23, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250423222433/https://aaup.sitehost.iu.edu/reports/AAUP_March_31_Letter_Shrivastav.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name=IPM>{{Cite web |last=Sandweiss |first=Ethan |title=Faculty group says IU violated policy when firing professor |url=https://indianapublicmedia.org/news/faculty-group-says-iu-violated-policy-when-firing-professor.php |access-date=April 1, 2025 |website=[[Indiana Public Media]] |language=en |archive-date=March 31, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250331213031/https://indianapublicmedia.org/news/faculty-group-says-iu-violated-policy-when-firing-professor.php |url-status=live |quote=IU removed webpages mentioning Wang on March 14, two weeks before the FBI search. Webpages mentioning his wife Nianli Ma, a staff member at IU Libraries, were deleted as well.}}</ref><ref name=FacultyOrgAlleges>{{cite web |url=https://www.idsnews.com/article/2025/03/xiaofeng-wang-aaup-iu-bloomington-policy |title=Faculty organization alleges IU violated policy in terminating Xiaofeng Wang |first=Andrew |last=Miller |website=[[Indiana Daily Student]]}}</ref> Later reports indicated that he was planning to leave IU to accept a position at a university in Singapore in June 2025 and had requested a leave of absence from the university in early March. The university had responded by putting him on administrative leave and locking him out of his office and laptop and disabling his email account before dismissing him by email a couple of weeks later.<ref name=dailystudent/><ref name=WiredFunding>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.wired.com/story/xiaofeng-wang-indiana-university-research-probe-china/ |title=Cybersecurity Professor Faced China-Funding Inquiry Before Disappearing, Sources Say |author=<!-- No byline --> |date=April 2, 2025 |magazine=[[Wired (magazine)|Wired]] |quote=Wang's new job offer 'would be irrelevant in any event because it is for [the] next academic year and would not justify firing him,' Tanford says. Terminating his employment via an email was a violation of university policy, Tanford claims, which prohibits firing a tenured professor without cause, and requires a 10-day notice and a hearing before a faculty board of review, if requested by the staff member.}}</ref> His union representative said that Wang's notification that he would be accepting a new position would not be a valid reason to fire him without allowing him to complete the current academic year as an IU faculty member.<ref name=WiredFunding/> He also said the university's policy prohibits firing a tenured professor by email or without cause and requires at least a 10-day notice and the opportunity for a hearing.<ref name=WiredFunding/> In cases without a finding of serious personal misconduct, the policy prescribes a one-year notice in writing before termination.<ref name=FacultyOrgAlleges/>

On April 2, 2025, 32 faculty members of the IU computer science department sent a letter to the university saying that Wang's "summary termination" was contrary to university policy and requesting the action to be revoked (19 by name and 13 anonymously). The letter said "Many of us are confused, saddened and frightened by the IU administration's actions." It acknowledged awareness that Wang is under investigation by law enforcement, but said "this alone cannot justify the termination of a tenured professor without following the due process to which all tenured faculty are entitled," and that "Treating a faculty colleague in this manner is undermining the university's ability to attract and retain high-caliber faculty members."<ref name=IPM3>{{cite web |url=https://indianapublicmedia.org/news/iu-computer-science-unit-speaks-about-fired-professor.php |title=IU computer science unit speaks about fired professor |last=Sandweiss |first=Ethan |website=[[Indiana Public Media]] |date=April 2, 2025 |access-date=April 16, 2025 |archive-date=April 5, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250405215733/https://indianapublicmedia.org/news/iu-computer-science-unit-speaks-about-fired-professor.php |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.idsnews.com/article/2025/04/iu-computer-science-condemn-wang-termination |title=IU computer science faculty condemn Xiaofeng Wang's termination in letter |first1=Jack |last1=Forrest |first2=Emerson |last2=Elledge |first3=Marissa |last3=Meador |first4=Andrew |last4=Miller |date=April 2, 2025 |website=[[Indiana Daily Student]]}}</ref>

On April 17, 2025, Yuzhen Ye, the chair of the IU computer science department, whose name was first on the faculty protest letter's list of signatories, spoke at a campus protest rally held for the National Day of Action to defend higher education (a national event in which 179 university campuses participated), and she questioned the evidence that appeared to have been the basis of the allegation that Wang had not properly disclosed funding information. She said that a researcher had applied for a 2017–2018 grant in China without Wang's knowledge, and that Wang had provided supporting information to the university in response to their investigation.<ref name=ChairSays/> She said the situation "really could have unfolded in a very different way if IU administration had chosen to trust its own faculty or give them a fair chance to respond".<ref name=ChairSays>{{cite web |url=https://indianapublicmedia.org/news/iu-department-chair-says-wang-didnt-know-about-chinese-grant.php |title=IU department chair says Wang didn't know about undisclosed Chinese research grant |date=April 17, 2025 |first=Ethan |last=Sandweiss |website=[[Indiana Public Media]] }}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> She said "I'm really saddened that IU just terminated someone's appointment after this many years of dedicated contribution to the school."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://indianapublicmedia.org/news/iu-bloomington-rallies-for-national-day-of-action-to-defend-higher-ed.php |title=Protest groups at IU unite for National Day of Action on higher education |date=April 17, 2025 |first=Ethan |last=Sandweiss |website=[[Indiana Public Media]] |access-date=April 18, 2025 |archive-date=April 18, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250418015244/https://indianapublicmedia.org/news/iu-bloomington-rallies-for-national-day-of-action-to-defend-higher-ed.php |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On May 2, 2025, more than 250 members of the university faculty and staff issued a letter criticizing the handling of Wang's firing, calling for the university to reinstate him to the faculty and to follow its policy of providing due process for faculty dismissals.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.idsnews.com/article/2025/05/faculty-staff-letter-to-provost-xiaofeng-wang-tenure-termination |title=Over 260 faculty, staff urge IU to undo Xiaofeng Wang's termination |first=Jack |last=Forrest |website=[[Indiana Daily Student]] |date=May 2, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |first=Aubrey |last=Wright |date=May 5, 2025 |url=https://indianapublicmedia.org/news/faculty-want-due-process-for-fired-cybersecurity-expert.php |title=IU faculty want due process for fired cybersecurity expert |website=[[Indiana Public Media]] |access-date=May 20, 2025 |archive-date=May 20, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250520061647/https://indianapublicmedia.org/news/faculty-want-due-process-for-fired-cybersecurity-expert.php |url-status=dead }}</ref>

US District Court judge [[Tanya Walton Pratt]] unsealed the search warrant applications for the raids on Wang's homes in early October 2025, revealing that the investigation claimed to be looking for evidence of research funding fraud by Wang. The affidavits used to establish probable cause for the search remained sealed.<ref name=IndyStarunsealed/> Pfefferkorn said the released information especially does not explain why Wang's wife was fired, since the warrant application contained no allegations against her. Pfefferkorn also noted that nothing indicated that Wang was being investigated for spying or was considered a threat to U.S. national security.<ref name=WFYIunsealed/> As of the time when the warrant information was released, no criminal charges had still been filed against either Wang or his wife, and neither of them were the subject of deportation proceedings.<ref name=WFYIunsealed>{{cite news |date=October 6, 2025 |title=Newly unsealed warrant shows search of fired IU professor's homes part of federal funding fraud investigation |first=George |last=Hale |work=[[WFYI (TV)|WFYI]] |url=https://www.wfyi.org/news/articles/newly-unsealed-warrant-shows-search-of-fired-iu-professors-homes-part-of-federal-funding-fraud-investigation |access-date=2025-11-18}}</ref><ref name=IndyStarunsealed>{{cite news |title=Unsealed documents reveal details behind FBI raid of fired Indiana University professor |first=Cate |last=Charron |work=[[The Indianapolis Star]] |date=October 6, 2025 |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/news/crime/2025/10/07/new-information-unsealed-about-fbi-raid-of-fired-chinese-iu-professor/86549294007/ |access-date=2025-11-18}}</ref>

== Honors ==
Wang was recognized as a [[fellow member|fellow]] of the [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers|IEEE]] in 2018, of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science|AAAS]] in 2022, and of the [[Association for Computing Machinery|ACM]] in 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Luddy's Wang receives ACM Fellow honor |url=https://news.luddy.indiana.edu/story.html?story=Luddy%E2%80%99s-Wang-receives-ACM-Fellow-honor |access-date=March 31, 2025 |website=Luddy School of Informatics, Computing, and Engineering: News Archive |language=en-US }}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Prior to their suspension and dismissal from IU, Wang lived in [[Bloomington, Indiana]], with his wife Ma Nianli (马念莉), who was a systems analyst and programmer at the IU Library Technologies division.<ref name=goodin-incommunicado/><ref name=heraldtimes/> They also had a home in [[Carmel, Indiana]], a northern suburb of [[Indianapolis]] about {{convert|70|mi|km|abbr=off|sp=us}} from the IU campus. The couple also has a son, who was born in Indiana and has launched a [[GoFundMe]] page to help fund his parents' legal defense.<ref name=IPM2/>
